lyric_idea: Bridge/outro (fast, repetitive build, 'just a little bit'): the fastest-escalating trend lines. Candidates show release cadence speeding up, the METR task-length curve running into its own measuring ceiling, and compute growing about 5x per year.

candidates.text: New models from Anthropic and OpenAI are arriving faster. Chart callouts: '70 days' (early 2024) to '11 days' ('median gap now').
candidates.speaker_or_outlet: Joshua Fonseca Rivera (@jfonsecarivera) on X; chart title as posted
candidates.verified_how: Deck source: capabilities manifest item 'jfonsecarivera-model-release-cadence-chart' (verified: true, quality 4) and 'chart-original' (quality 5); slide_capabilities.js cadenceSlide() shows the same chart. Opened the local JPG and read the title and callouts. Post text and engagement come from the deck's rev3/post.json notes (api.fxtwitter.com, Oct 5, 2026). Deck's own re-count: 10.5-day median over Apr 5 to Oct 5, 2026 (14 gaps, from vendor launch pages); flagship-only 14.5 days. The on-screen text is the chart's own title and callouts, not the lyric.
candidates.why_it_fits: The single most direct 'arriving faster' image in the research set. The 70 to 11 drop is visually a steep fall that can be animated during the fast build, and the title alone reads in about 2 s. Caveat for the edit: it is one researcher's chart (his bio says Anthropic safety fellow), method not stated, not an official statistic. Say so on screen or in the voiceover.

candidates.text: Length of software tasks that different LLMs can complete 50% of the time. Band label: 'Measurements above 16 hrs are unreliable with our current task suite'.
candidates.verified_how: Deck source: capabilities manifest 'metr-time-horizon-chart' (verified: true, quality 5), plus 'metr-th-page-chart-with-date' and 'metr-th-page-chart-band' (rev2/metr-th-page-chart-unreliable-band.png). Opened the local PNG and read the title and the hatched band text. Deck notes say metr.org/time-horizons still reads 'LAST UPDATED May 8, 2026' (checked Oct 4, 2026). candidates.why_it_fits: The hatched 'unreliable above 16 hrs' band is the ego joke in one frame: the most-watched graph in AI runs out of ruler at the top. Pairs with the broken-ego idea. The curve climbs steeply through the build. Use METR's exact title, not the deck's 'doubles every ~4 months' wording.

candidates.text: Training compute for frontier language models has been growing at 5× per year since 2020.
candidates.verified_how: Deck source: splash manifest 'epoch-trends-page-screenshot' (verified: true) and 'epoch-trends-quote-5x-since-2020' (verified: true, verbatim, Trends page updated Feb. 5, 2026); splash/scaling-epoch-trend.json. Deck notes also cite 'doubling every 5.2 months since 2020' on the same page (not visible in the screenshot, so not verified by me). Use the '×' sign as the page prints it.
candidates.why_it_fits: The compute growth beat: a stat that reads as a steady exponential. Pairs with the METR doubling line in the build. Caveat: it covers frontier language-model training compute and is a 4-6x range, not a single fixed rate.
